name: Vertical Press
definition: A shoulder-oriented compound press whose strict concentric phase elevates the humerus in a front or scapular path through shoulder flexion and abduction, scapular upward rotation and posterior tilt, and elbow extension. Open-chain presses move an external implement 75 to 90 degrees superior to horizontal; the reviewed closed-chain branch is a strict wall-supported handstand push-up that moves the body between a fifteen-centimeter head target and full elbow-and-shoulder extension. Li et al. directly establish its inversion-stand spacing, feet-only wall contact, forty-second maximum-repetition test, and no-waist-collapse or bent-leg validity rules, but do not measure joint, scapular, or muscle actions. The existing vertical-press signature and mover hierarchy are therefore an explicit mechanics transfer, while Kinoshita et al. support only the static handstand stability environment. The five-repetition product seed is not a source prescription. High-incline, landmine, rotating Arnold, behind-neck, leg-driven push-press or jerk, cable, pike, freestanding, parallettes, deficit, and kipping variants remain outside this family.

exerciseRules.description: Machine vertical presses use a constrained load path and declare the machine mechanism.
Non-machine vertical presses are not constrained by machine rails or levers and do not declare a machine mechanism.
A kettlebell vertical press uses a neutral grip and declares the standard bell-down orientation; bottom-up pressing remains outside this contract.
Only kettlebell presses declare a bell orientation.
A press without posterior torso support permits free scapular translation and explicitly declares spinal stabilization, including the reviewed inverted branch.
A bench or machine pad requires a seated press and limits scapular translation without removing upward rotation or posterior tilt.
A strict standing press has no posterior torso support, stays at 90 degrees, and explicitly declares spinal and pelvic stabilization.
A unilateral press explicitly declares spinal and pelvic stability demands created by the asymmetric load.
The currently admitted straight-bar vertical press uses a pronated grip; neutral specialty bars require a future contract review.
A standard straight-bar vertical press is bilateral; unilateral bar-like implements require a different equipment type and review.
A Smith vertical press uses a pronated grip beneath the rails but may be standing or seated.
The admitted Smith press uses both hands on the standard bar; an asymmetrically loaded one-arm rail press is outside this contract.
The machinePad support value belongs only to a purpose-built shoulder-press machine, not a free-weight or Smith bench setup.
A converging shoulder-press machine is seated against its pad and uses its canonical neutral handles.
The exact MTSSP record uses one independent arm and its working-side stack; its source identifies a shoulder-press path but does not report grip orientation or a numeric inclination.
The MTSSP fixture identity cannot be attached to a generic or linked shoulder press.
Records outside the exact independent MTS mechanism cannot carry its fixture or load-history axes.
Existing front and scapular press records retain their explicit numeric geometry.
The inverted press record retains its explicit numeric geometry.
The source-unreported grip marker belongs only to the exact MTSSP record.
The manufacturer shoulder-press path marker belongs only to the exact MTSSP record.
The independent-arm marker belongs only to the MTSSP mechanism.
The one-arm sequence marker belongs only to the MTSSP mechanism.
The working-side stack convention belongs only to the MTSSP mechanism.
The equal per-side stack convention belongs only to the MTSSP mechanism.
The only reviewed bodyweight branch is the bilateral strict wall-supported handstand push-up with exact inversion-stand geometry, feet-only wall contact, and no kipping or body collapse.
Open-chain external-load presses do not declare the exact wall-supported handstand fixture axes.

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold the bar at your upper chest with your palms facing forward and your hands just outside shoulder width.
execution.movement: Press the bar overhead, letting your shoulder blades move naturally, and move your head only enough to clear the bar.
execution.endpoint: Finish with your elbows straight and the bar balanced over the middle of your feet.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the bar under control to your upper chest.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your hips and knees motionless.
execution.supportAndPosture: Brace your trunk without leaning back.
disqualifyingCompensations: Driving through the hips or knees turns the strict press into a push press.
Leaning back turns the vertical press into an incline press.

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with your palms facing forward and your elbows slightly forward of your torso.
execution.movement: Press both dumbbells overhead along slightly forward paths without turning your hands or leaning back, and let your shoulder blades move naturally.
execution.endpoint: Finish with your elbows straight and the weights balanced over your body.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the dumbbells under control to shoulder height.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your hips and knees motionless and your hands unturned.
execution.supportAndPosture: Brace your trunk without leaning back.
disqualifyingCompensations: Driving through the hips or knees turns the strict press into a push press.
Leaning back turns the vertical press into an incline press.

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell at the shoulder you are working, with your palm facing forward and your elbow slightly forward.
execution.movement: Press the dumbbell overhead on a slightly forward path without turning your hand, leaning sideways or back, or twisting, and let your shoulder blade move naturally.
execution.endpoint: Finish with your elbow straight and the weight balanced over your body.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the dumbbell under control to the shoulder.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your hips level and facing forward, and do not bend your hips or knees.
execution.supportAndPosture: Brace your torso without leaning sideways or back.
disqualifyingCompensations: Driving through the hips or knees turns the strict press into a push press.
Leaning sideways turns the one-arm press into a side-bent push.
Twisting the torso turns the press into a rotational push.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish the set on the working side before changing sides.

execution.startingPosition: Set the bench backrest to about 85 degrees and sit with your pelvis and upper torso supported and your feet planted. Hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with your palms facing forward and your elbows slightly forward of your torso.
execution.movement: Press both dumbbells overhead along slightly forward paths without turning your hands, pushing through your legs, or lifting your torso from the bench.
execution.endpoint: Let your shoulder blades move as much as the backrest allows, and finish with your elbows straight.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the dumbbells under control to shoulder height.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your hands unturned and your legs quiet.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your pelvis and upper torso supported on the bench with your feet planted.
disqualifyingCompensations: Pushing through the legs turns the seated press into a leg-assisted press.
Lifting the torso off the bench turns the supported press into an unsupported press.

execution.startingPosition: Set a bench backrest to about 80 degrees inside a rack and sit with your pelvis and upper torso supported and your feet planted. Unrack the bar at your upper chest with your palms facing forward and your hands just outside shoulder width.
execution.movement: Press the bar overhead in front of your head without pushing through your legs or lifting your torso from the bench, and let your shoulder blades move naturally.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the bar under control to your upper chest.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your legs quiet throughout the press.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your pelvis and upper torso supported on the bench with your feet planted.
disqualifyingCompensations: Pushing through the legs turns the seated press into a leg-assisted press.
Lifting the torso off the bench turns the supported press into an unsupported press.

exercises.name: Unsupported Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
aliases: Seated Dumbbell Press Without Back Support

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright on a flat bench without a backrest, plant your feet, and hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with your palms facing forward.
execution.movement: Press both dumbbells overhead along slightly forward paths without leaning back, pushing through your legs, or turning your hands.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the dumbbells under control to shoulder height.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your hands unturned and your legs quiet.
execution.supportAndPosture: Brace your trunk so your ribs stay stacked over your pelvis.
disqualifyingCompensations: Leaning back turns the unsupported seated press into a reclined press.
Pushing through the legs turns the seated press into a leg-assisted press.

execution.startingPosition: Set the bench backrest to about 75 degrees and sit with your upper torso and pelvis supported and your feet planted. Hold one dumbbell at the shoulder you are working with your palm facing inward.
execution.movement: Press the dumbbell overhead on a slightly forward path without turning your hand, pushing through your legs, twisting, or leaning sideways, while keeping both hips on the bench.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the dumbbell under control to the shoulder.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your hand unturned and your legs quiet.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your upper torso, pelvis, and both hips supported on the bench with your feet planted.
disqualifyingCompensations: Leaning sideways turns the one-arm press into a side-bent push.
Twisting the torso turns the press into a rotational push.
Pushing through the legs turns the seated press into a leg-assisted press.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish the set on the working side, then repeat on the other side.

execution.startingPosition: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold one kettlebell at your working shoulder with your wrist straight and the bell resting against your forearm.
execution.movement: Press the kettlebell overhead on a slightly forward path without letting it flip upside down, leaning, or twisting.
execution.endpoint: Finish with your elbow straight and your forearm vertical.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the kettlebell under control to the rack.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your hips and knees motionless and your wrist straight.
execution.supportAndPosture: Brace your trunk without leaning or twisting.
disqualifyingCompensations: Letting the bell flip upside down turns the standard press into a bottom-up press.
Driving through the hips or knees turns the strict press into a push press.
Leaning or twisting turns the one-arm press into a side-bent push.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish the set on the working side before changing sides.

execution.startingPosition: Place an upright bench under the Smith bar so the rails keep the bar in front of your head, set the backrest to about 85 degrees, and sit with your torso supported and your feet planted. Unhook the bar at your upper chest with your palms facing forward and your hands just outside shoulder width.
execution.movement: Press along the rails without pushing through your legs or lifting from the bench.
execution.returnPhase: Lower the bar under control and rehook it securely.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your legs quiet throughout the press.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your torso supported on the bench with your feet planted.
disqualifyingCompensations: Pushing through the legs turns the seated press into a leg-assisted press.
Lifting the torso off the bench turns the supported press into an unsupported press.

execution.startingPosition: Adjust the seat so the handles begin near shoulder height with your palms facing each other, then sit against the machine pad with your feet planted.
execution.movement: Press both lever arms overhead along their converging front paths without pushing through your legs or lifting from the pad.
execution.endpoint: Finish with your elbows straight without forcing your shoulders forward.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your legs quiet throughout the press.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep your torso against the machine pad with your feet planted.
disqualifyingCompensations: Pushing through the legs turns the seated press into a leg-assisted press.
Lifting the torso off the pad turns the supported press into an unsupported press.

exercises.name: Hammer Strength MTSSP Single-Arm Shoulder Press

execution.sideOrDirection: Use the same selected stack value on both sides, enter that per-working-side value once, complete all repetitions with one arm, then repeat on the other side.
execution.startingPosition: On the Hammer Strength MTSSP only, adjust the seat and select the equal per-side load. Let the unused pivot-away grip remain clear and compare history only on this fixture.
execution.movement: Press one independent arm upward through the manufacturer's shoulder-press path while keeping the torso against the pad.
execution.endpoint: Finish at the comfortable machine-defined endpoint without forcing the shoulder forward.
execution.returnPhase: Return the working arm alone under control through its diverging path.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the non-working arm still and resist trunk rotation or lateral lean.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the pelvis and torso against the machine support with both feet planted and no leg drive.
disqualifyingCompensations: Moving both independent arms changes the one-arm history.
Using unequal stack settings cannot be represented by this one-value history.
Adding the two stack selections together changes the working-side load meaning.
Leaning or lifting from the pad adds trunk momentum.

execution.startingPosition: Place the handstand supports 10 cm from a wall and 20 cm wider than your shoulders, with a 15 cm sponge centered beneath your head. Kick up into a handstand and let only your feet touch the wall gently.
execution.movement: Lower until your head contacts the sponge.
execution.endpoint: Press until your arms are straight overhead without folding at your waist, bending your knees, swinging for momentum, or pushing off the wall.
execution.returnPhase: Lower under control until your head contacts the sponge again.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your knees straight and your waist firm throughout the repetition.
execution.supportAndPosture: Let only your feet touch the wall gently while you stay stacked over your hands. Perform as many controlled repetitions as you can in 40 seconds; five repetitions is only a suggested starting target. Count only repetitions that follow the setup and movement rules above.
disqualifyingCompensations: Folding at the waist turns the strict handstand push-up into a pike push-up.
Bending the knees or swinging turns the strict repetition into a kipping push-up.
Pushing off the wall turns the wall-supported repetition into a wall-assisted climb.
